mechanism_narrative: A higher-than-average federal funds rate (indicating a tightening monetary policy) compresses equity valuations by increasing the discount rate applied to future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.0% over a 3-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE > 5.0% for 3 months), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a negative feedback loop in corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (characterized by high industrial production growth and low unemployment), a further acceleration in industrial production signals overcapacity and potential profit margin compression, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion when INDPRO growth accelerates, or the Rank IC for the regime-specific signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the year-over-year CPI inflation rate above 2.5% signals rising inflation expectations, which prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS growth is positive, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market recovery regime (characterized by rising housing starts and low mortgage rates), a decline in housing starts signals a weakening in the housing sector, which reduces consumer confidence and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during housing market recovery when HOUST declines, or the Rank IC for the regime-specific signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a broad-based economic contraction, which triggers a negative feedback loop in corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where both INDPRO and GDPC1 decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
